title: ECB Launches Investigation After Brydon Carse Handcuffed Outside Derby Nightclub
excerpt: England fast bowler was briefly detained by police following a dispute with bouncers, adding to a string of nightlife incidents plaguing English cricket.
body:
• England fast bowler Brydon Carse was handcuffed by police outside a nightclub in Derby on Saturday night and is now under investigation by the ECB.
  • Carse was briefly detained following a dispute with bouncers over re-entry but was not arrested and returned to his team hotel without charge.
  • England teammates Matthew Potts and Ben Stokes were visible in video footage circulating on social media, though Carse was not on England duty at the time.
  • The incident adds to a troubled pattern of nightlife controversies involving England cricketers over the past year, including episodes involving Harry Brook and Stokes himself.

Police Intervene After Nightclub Dispute

The England and Wales Cricket Board has launched an investigation after fast bowler Brydon Carse was handcuffed by police outside a nightclub in Derby on Saturday night, the latest in a series of off-field incidents to hit English cricket.

Video footage circulating on social media showed the 31-year-old Durham bowler surrounded by four police officers outside the venue. He was briefly restrained but not formally arrested, according to multiple reports. Carse returned to the team hotel after being released without charge.

"We are aware of an incident which is reported to have taken place in Derby last night, and are currently investigating. We will provide a further update when possible."

— ECB spokesperson

The incident is understood to have stemmed from a dispute with nightclub bouncers over re-entering the venue after Carse briefly stepped outside. England and Durham teammate Matthew Potts was seen in the footage attempting to speak with Carse, while former England captain Ben Stokes was also visible in the background.

Celebrating a County Championship Win

Carse was not on England duty at the time. He had been released from the Test squad — where he was an unused member for the first Test against Pakistan at Headingley, which England won by an innings and 103 runs inside three days — to play for Durham in the County Championship.

Durham beat Derbyshire by 338 runs at Derby, with Stokes taking 5-17 as the hosts were bowled out for 84. Carse contributed two wickets. Members of the Durham squad went out in Derby to celebrate the emphatic victory, with the evening ending on a sour note.

Carse remains in England's squad for the second Test against Pakistan at Lord's, starting Thursday. The team assembles in London on Monday.

A Familiar Pattern for England Cricket

The Derby incident lands against a backdrop of repeated nightlife controversies that have dogged the England team. Last November, Harry Brook, England's white-ball captain, was punched by a security guard in Wellington hours before leading the team in an ODI against New Zealand.

During the Ashes earlier this year, a mid-series break in Noosa generated headlines over players' drinking. Most recently, Stokes and Gus Atkinson were suspended from the second New Zealand Test after breaching a midnight curfew at a London nightclub — an incident that precipitated Stokes' retirement from international cricket and Joe Root's reinstatement as captain.

Root subsequently scrapped the enforced curfew, calling on players to "be adults." The Derby footage suggests that message has not yet fully landed.

Carse's Turbulent Recent History

The South Africa-born fast bowler has endured a difficult period off the field. In 2024, Carse received a three-month suspension from the Cricket Regulator for placing 303 bets on cricket matches between 2017 and 2019, a breach of ECB anti-corruption regulations.

On the pitch, Carse was England's leading wicket-taker during the 2025-26 Ashes, which England lost 4-1. He has represented England in 14 Tests and 44 white-ball matches across his five-year international career, regularly clocking speeds around 91 mph.

The ECB and Cricket Regulator are both expected to investigate despite the incident occurring when Carse was not on England duty. Whether any disciplinary action follows could affect his availability for the remainder of the Pakistan series.

What Happens Next

England's second Test against Pakistan begins at Lord's on Thursday. Carse is expected to remain in the squad, though his prospects of being selected for the playing XI — having been unused at Headingley — may now be complicated by the investigation. The ECB has said it will provide further updates when possible.
